report.headline: Usage projected to jump from 16.1% in the NBA to 23.0% in the EuroLeague, but the shooting-efficiency projection is unreliable and the usage range spans nearly two standard deviations of the league.

projection.text: The model projects a 23.0% usage rate in the EuroLeague, up from a 16.1% usage rate in the NBA (0.82 sd below the NBA average that season), and above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.4% (sd 4.2%).

risks.text: The true shooting projection should not be relied upon: the model's 4.5% mean absolute error is worse than the 4.3% achieved by simply guessing the league average, over the same 277-transition evaluation.

The 95% prediction interval for usage rate (16.7%-29.3%) covers more than three standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution, meaning the model can say the player will likely take an above-average share of possessions but cannot pin down where within a broad band.

The subject entered the NBA source season at 16.1% usage, 0.82 sd below the NBA average, a larger deficit than the -0.31 sd average standing of players who historically made this move, which is a departure from the typical mover profile the model is fitted on.

The true shooting standing was also below the NBA average (53.0%, -0.20 sd), and while the projection lands near the EuroLeague mean, the wide 80% and 95% intervals combined with the baseline failure mean this efficiency figure has essentially no demonstrated predictive value here.

strengths.text: Projected usage of 23.0% represents a large increase over the 16.1% NBA usage rate and sits above the EuroLeague average of 20.4%, consistent with the general pattern of expanded roles for NBA-to-EuroLeague movers.

For usage rate specifically, the model beats the best trivial baseline (3.2% mean absolute error vs 4.2% for the league-mean baseline over 277 held-out transitions), so the usage projection carries real signal.

The fitted NBA->EL slope on usage rate alone is 0.977, indicating that a player's standing relative to their league carries across almost fully on this metric, over a base of 115 historical transitions.
Projected true shooting of 55.4% is close to the EuroLeague average of 56.3%, suggesting no expected efficiency collapse even though the metric itself is not trustworthy in isolation.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 18.9% to 27.1%, an 8.2-point band that is roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution; the 95% interval widens further to 16.7%-29.3%. The true shooting projection of 55.4% carries a comparably wide 80% interval (47.9%-62.9%) and a 95% interval of 43.9%-66.9%, but that projection is built on a model that loses to the simple league-average baseline (4.5% error vs 4.3% for the baseline), so it should not be treated as informative.
